title: Cascade Failure Prevention
summary: Contain overload and dependency failures so one slow tool or model does not consume the capacity of an entire agent platform.
overview: Cascade prevention limits the propagation of failure across queues, retries, threads, connection pools, and downstream services. Agent workflows amplify this risk through fan-out: one user request may create several model calls and many tool operations. When a dependency slows, in-flight work grows; retries then add load precisely when less capacity is available.

The control system needs several cooperating boundaries. Deadlines cap waiting, bulkheads isolate capacity, circuit breakers stop repeated calls to failing dependencies, admission control bounds demand, and graceful degradation reduces optional work. Each boundary must preserve enough information to distinguish rejected work from work whose external outcome is uncertain.

production.poc: A prototype should count downstream calls per task and deliberately slow a tool to reveal unbounded fan-out.
production.production: Production introduces end-to-end deadlines, retry budgets, concurrency isolation, and overload responses before queues saturate.
production.scale: At scale, model regional failures, synchronize neither retries nor recovery probes, and reserve capacity for critical tenants and administrative recovery paths.

components.name: Admission controller
components.role: Rejects or defers work before local resources are exhausted.

components.name: Bulkhead pools
components.role: Separate concurrency budgets by dependency or workload priority.

components.name: Circuit breaker
components.role: Uses recent outcomes to stop calls and permit limited recovery probes.

components.name: Deadline propagator
components.role: Carries remaining time through nested operations and cancels expired work.

components.name: Retry budget
components.role: Caps additional attempts across the entire logical request.

flow.title: Estimate fan-out
flow.description: Calculate whether the requested plan fits remaining time and downstream capacity.

flow.title: Acquire isolated capacity
flow.description: Reserve a slot in the relevant dependency pool rather than a shared unlimited executor.

flow.title: Check breaker state
flow.description: Fail fast or choose an approved fallback when a dependency is known to be unhealthy.

flow.title: Execute within deadline
flow.description: Propagate cancellation and avoid starting work that cannot finish within the request budget.

flow.title: Retry within budget
flow.description: Apply bounded backoff with jitter only for eligible failures and known-safe effects.

flow.title: Recover gradually
flow.description: Allow limited probes and ramp traffic after sustained evidence of recovery.

useCase.title: Storm-driven service requests
useCase.situation: A utility assistant handles outage reports, account inquiries, and restoration explanations during severe weather.
useCase.problem: A slow account API causes retries and consumes worker slots needed for outage reporting.
useCase.requirement: Keep critical outage intake available while nonessential enrichment degrades.
useCase.architecture: Separate pools protect outage intake, and the account adapter uses a breaker with a shared retry budget.
runtime: The account pool fills and new account enrichment is deferred.
Outage tasks continue through their reserved capacity while a small probe stream checks account recovery.
useCase.failure: If the breaker closes too aggressively, fresh failures reopen it and the recovery ramp pauses.
useCase.impact: Track rejected optional work, protected-task latency, concurrency saturation, and retry amplification; a healthy platform may intentionally serve fewer noncritical features.

tradeoffs.cost: Some requests are rejected despite a running process.
Require capacity allocation and can reduce sharing efficiency.
Bad thresholds can delay recovery or oscillate.

failures.detection: Downstream attempts greatly exceed original request volume.
failures.recovery: Assign one retry owner and enforce a request-wide budget.

failures.detection: Many replicas probe or reconnect simultaneously.
failures.recovery: Add jitter, cap probe concurrency, and ramp accepted traffic.

mistakes.fix: Stop expired downstream work where supported.

mistakes.mistake: Sharing one executor for all tools
mistakes.fix: Separate critical and optional dependency capacity.
Classify errors and reconcile ambiguous effects before replay.

whenToUse: Use for fan-out workflows and shared dependencies.
Use where traffic surges threaten critical operations.
Use when retries contribute materially to resource use.
whenNotToUse: Avoid breaker complexity around trivial local functions.
Do not fail open across authorization boundaries.
Do not shed critical work without a documented deferred path.
checklist: Measure downstream calls per original request.
Load-test degradation and recovery, not only steady state.
